28. ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY IN PREGNANCY

•1.4% of obstetric admission.
•e GFR – Not reliable.
•Serum creatinine decreases in pregnancy by 35 µmol/l.
•Average = 53 µmol /l.
•Abnormal >90 µmol/l => investigate.
•40% AKI – unrecognized.
•Most common cause = Pre-eclampsia.

Management:

1.Fluid status Assessment.
2.Medication review.
3.Fluid replacement.
4.Diagnostic work – up.
5.Involvement of nephrologist if initial management is failed.

Drug dosage Adjustment:

-Antibiotics.
-Anticoagulants.
-Insulin.
-Opiates.

If GFR < 30.

•NSAIDS => C/I in:
1.AKI.
2.CKD.
3.PTE.
4.Volume depletion.
5.Asthma.

Urea – teratogenic >17mmol/l => despite medical treatment need Renal replacement therapy.

⇨Pre – Eclampsia:
•Leads to AKI in 1.5 – 2% cases.

Biopsy shows:

•Endotheliosis.

Mgso4:

•Renal execration.
•If Urine output <20ml/hour or creatinine >90 then
1.Give only 50% dose of Mgso4.
2.Mgso4 level monitoring 4 – 6 hourly.

Maintain levels 2 – 3.5mol/lit.

Post-partum diuresis (normal).

36 – 48 hours.

Before diuresis, oliguria is normal.

•Cause AKI – 3 – 15%.

Then recover

⇨SLE:
•20 – 49% - renal involvement.
•16% renal disease activation in pregnancy.
•10% of lupus nephrites develop ARF in pregnancy.
⇨Obstructive Nephropathy:
•Pelvicalyceal system + ureteral dilatation are normal in pregnancy.
•Pathological if:
1.Dilatation of urethra distal to Brim.
2.Ureteric jet absents.
3.Obstruction don’t disappear by positioning the women on all four.
⇨Drugs:
•Penicillin
•Cephalosporins
•PPI

Common drugs and their effects on kidneys:

1.Naproxen – AKI.
2.Indomethacin nephrotoxicity – nephritis, hyperkalemia.
3.Fenoprofen – nephritis.
4.Meloxicam – very little renal effects.

Adverse Effects of NSAIDS:

 

GI:

1.Dyspepsia
2.Ulceration.
3.Bleeding
4.Colonic stricture

Renal:

1.AKI
2.Hyperkalemia 10 – 46%.
3.Na retention.
4.Interstitial nephritis.
5.Papillary necrosis.
